title: Pinned real Ribasim conflict between 6-hour BMI management calls and 1-hour saveat allocation boundaries

sequencing.rationale: Freeze the clock-conflict hypothesis before observing the no-scarcity negative control or BMI-owned-clock experiment.

source_binding.allocation_time: AllocationTime seeds allocation tstops from solver.saveat.
source_binding.bmi_update_until: BMI.update_until adds its requested endpoint as an allocation tstop but does not remove existing saveat-derived tstops.
source_binding.expected_precedence: The union of boundaries governs allocation; therefore a finer saveat grid remains active inside coarser BMI coupling windows.

purpose: Test whether a coupler can impose a 6-hour management clock when solver.saveat remains finer at 1 hour. This is the conflict counterpart to DUMMY-19I.
hypotheses: Calling BMI.update_until at 6-hour endpoints does not suppress the pre-existing 1-hour saveat-derived allocation tstops.
allocation_data contains 24 hourly allocation records, not four 6-hour records.
Both priority cases reach full 40/20 allocation after repeated hourly state-feedback optimization.
One-day physical recipient volumes and Basin endpoint match the independently frozen 1-hour hybrid reference from the preregistered DUMMY-19G sweep.
The result is materially distinct from the 6-hour reference that DUMMY-19I is designed to test with daily saveat.
A coupler therefore cannot claim exclusive ownership of a coarser management clock while solver.saveat introduces finer allocation boundaries in this pinned implementation.
forbidden: no changing saveat or BMI endpoints after execution
no replacing the 1-hour preregistered hybrid reference with observed DUMMY-19G values
no claim that saveat is semantically intended as a management clock
no production prescription before the clock contract is explicitly resolved

authority_rebind.meaning: Execution rebound after DUMMY-19I2. The prospectively frozen 1-hour versus 6-hour clock-conflict model, reference and tolerances are unchanged.
